clue.text: Thirty seconds initially spent framing paintings of birds

indicators.note: framing means the first pieces go around the paintings, like a frame

parts.note: half a minute, and MIN is the first half of the word minute
paintings are works of art, ART

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word spent

explanation.surface: Someone spends their first half-minute putting frames round some bird pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty seconds' is not a time abbreviation but half of the word minute. 'framing' wraps the first pieces round the paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: House martins and sand martins are small swallow-like songbirds.

clue.text: Poor treatment partly makes us immigrants rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
partly means only a portion of the words makes us immigrants is used

explanation.surface: A political complaint that immigrants are badly treated and their numbers keep going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' picks ESUSIM out of 'makES US IMmigrants'; 'rise' turns it round, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse is abuse or improper handling, a kind of poor treatment.

clue.text: Trashed uniform adopted by leftie

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into the family, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a leftie is a socialist, a Red

indicators.note: the second half of the word uniform, read as the verb form, says to shape the first half into new order

parts.note: the first three letters of the word uniform, taken as they are

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist has wrecked a uniform they were given.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'uniform' does two jobs: its first half is the fodder and 'form' is the anagram signal; 'adopted by' then puts the result inside the leftie.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trashed has been wrecked or spoilt beyond use, which is to say ruined.

clue.text: Dietitian upset about slimmer's heart scare

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of dietitian are rearranged
a word's heart is its middle letter, here taken from slimmer

explanation.surface: A dieter is distressed by a dietitian who has a fright about their progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DIETITIAN, and 'about' wraps it round M, the middle letter of SLIMMER ('heart').
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate someone is to frighten or cow them, so it is a verb meaning to scare.

clue.text: It's a wobbly rooftop step

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and shaken about, so the letters of it's a are jumbled

parts.note: the top of the word roof is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A loose step up on the roof is a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' is the anagram signal, and 'rooftop' means the top letter of roof, not a roof's peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a staircase.

clue.text: Almonds one scattered around mountains produce fruit

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters are put round the next piece
scattered means thrown about, so the letters of almonds one are rearranged

parts.note: mountain ranges, RANGES

explanation.surface: A grower scatters almonds near some hills and they yield fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges ALMONDS ONE, and 'around' wraps those letters round RANGES. The answer is also the old London nursery rhyme behind the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges and lemons are both citrus fruits, so the pair is fruit.

clue.text: India gripped by guns as ritual

indicators.note: gripped by means held tightly inside the following piece

parts.note: ordnance is military artillery, big guns
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: In India, guns are held as part of a ceremonial ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance can be a religious rite or ceremony, as well as a decree.

clue.text: Even members of yacht team excuse me!

indicators.note: even members means the second, fourth and other even-numbered letters of each word

explanation.surface: A yacht's crew interrupts politely to get attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters are taken word by word: yAcHt gives AH, tEaM gives EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the throat-clearing sound made to catch attention, a polite interruption.

clue.text: Starts to get out of drowning in debt — expert advice is a useful suggestion

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Getting financial guidance to escape crushing debt is a sensible plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of eight words in a row spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A good idea is a helpful or worthwhile proposal.

clue.text: Anxious uncertainty getting lift could develop into spitefulness

indicators.note: could develop into means the answer's letters with those of lift may be reworked into the word spitefulness

explanation.surface: Worrying over a promised boost might turn into resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus LIFT rearranges to SPITEFULNESS, as 'could develop into' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense state of waiting anxiously for an outcome.

clue.text: Church's bouncy castle isn't for grown-ups to enter

indicators.note: to enter means the next piece goes inside the rearranged letters
a bouncy thing jumps about, so the letters of castle and isn't are rearranged

parts.note: grown-ups are adults, here men

explanation.surface: A church fete's inflatable castle is strictly for children only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncy' is the anagram signal on 'castle isn't', and 'to enter' places the grown-ups inside. St Clement's is the London church of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: St Clement's is a London church, so the name stands for the church's own.

clue.text: See 5
Mates unhappy with Jeremy? They decrease

indicators.note: unhappy means out of sorts, so the letters of mates are rearranged

parts.note: Jeremy Irons is a well-known English actor

explanation.surface: Friends are miserable with Jeremy because their numbers are falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' rearranges MATES to STEAM. 'decrease' is read as de-crease: steam irons take creases out.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron removes wrinkles from fabric, so it literally de-creases clothes.

clue.text: No 7 assistant

indicators.note: No 7 reads as no-good idea, and something no good is botched, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: entry 7 is a good idea; dropping good leaves the word idea

explanation.surface: A numbered helper, like a team's No 7, assists.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is GOOD IDEA, so 'No 7' is a no-good IDEA: an IDEA made badly, so its letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: Trustworthy English writer turning naughty, led off outside

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the rest
off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of led are rearranged

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool

indicators.note: turning means the word for naughty is read backwards

parts.note: naughty means bad

explanation.surface: An English author goes bad after being led astray from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns LED into D...LE, which goes 'outside' E, PEN and DAB (BAD, 'turning').
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependable can be relied on, which is what trustworthy means.

clue.text: Like the centre of Bordeaux, without barriers and without weapons

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, here the two central letters of Bordeaux

parts.note: a place without barriers has no fences, it is fenceless

explanation.surface: Central Bordeaux, like an open city, has no walls and no arms.
explanation.walkthrough: BORDEAUX has eight letters, so its centre is DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenceless means unprotected, with no arms or means of defence.

clue.text: See 24
See 9
Schedule inverted by a sod of a troublemaker

parts.note: sod and git are both mild British insults for an annoying person

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so the word for schedule is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: Some awkward so-and-so has turned the timetable upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' reverses the schedule word. Git and sod are both British slang for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up unrest, a troublemaker by trade.

clue.text: Force two to pick up easily digestible French cheeses

parts.note: a light meal is easy to digest

indicators.note: to pick up means to hear, so the word for French cheeses is given by its sound

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese; bries are several

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up some mild, easily digested French cheeses.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIES spoken sounds like BREEZE. Force two is a wind strength on the Beaufort scale.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Beaufort wind scale, force two is officially named a light breeze.

clue.text: Record reader and writer

definitions.meaning: the needle that tracks the groove of a vinyl record
a pointed writing tool, as used on wax tablets

explanation.surface: A record player and a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the gramophone needle and the ancient pointed pen are called a stylus.

clue.text: Member of Trinity reported in newspaper

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the answer is what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: the Holy Trinity is Father, Son and Holy Spirit, so one member is the Son

explanation.surface: A Trinity College fellow features in a press report.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SON said out loud is THE SUN, a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a popular British daily tabloid newspaper.

clue.text: Limited containment of bug

indicators.note: containment means the answer is held within the letters of the word limited

explanation.surface: Only limited measures to contain an outbreak of a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a tiny arachnid, loosely called a bug.

clue.text: Waterside dump in London

definitions.note: a place in London: the definition describes the district by its location

parts.note: the shore is land beside the sea or a lake
to ditch something is to dump it

explanation.surface: A grubby tip by the river somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoreditch is an East London district, and its bells appear in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreditch is an area of the East End, one that lies inside the capital.

clue.text: Taken again by shocker heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a Taser is an electric stun gun that shocks its target

explanation.surface: Police with a stun gun detain someone a second time while going north.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam that was resat has been sat or taken again.

clue.text: Distant object in game is your debt, according to the 26 of 9 1 across

definitions.text: your debt, according to the 26 of 9 1 across

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the word for a game

parts.note: fives is a British handball game played in a walled court
distant means far
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A faraway target during a match costs you a debt of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a ball game hit with the hand against walls. The rhyme says 'You owe me five farthings, say the bells of St Martin's'; a farthing was an old quarter-penny.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the bells of St Martin's say the hearer owes them five farthings.

clue.text: Sustenance for worried nit nurse? About time!

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
worried means agitated, so the letters of nit nurse are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school nit nurse, fretting, is finally getting something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges NIT NURSE, and 'About' puts it round T. A nit nurse checks schoolchildren for head lice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrients are the nourishing substances in food, which is sustenance.

clue.text: Inventor's clangers

definitions.meaning: ..., belonging to Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone

explanation.surface: An inventor's blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clangers' sounds like mistakes (a British word for a blunder), but here it means things that ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell was an inventor, and bells literally make clanging sounds.

clue.text: One is overwhelmed by ogre's howls

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped, so the first piece ends up inside the next

parts.note: Shrek is the ogre of the animated films; Shrek's is the possessive
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A villager is overwhelmed by the howling of an ogre.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieks are high piercing cries, much like howls or screams.

clue.text: Twit's betrayal

parts.note: the first letter of the word Twit, taken as it is
wit is reason or good sense

explanation.surface: A fool's act of treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twit' splits as T + WIT, and wit is REASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or ruler.
